channel.title: GTA VI PC race - Updates
channel.description: Unofficial RSS feed of the updates log at https://vuyp.github.io/gta6-pc-race/#updates

item.title: Vice-Tay rebuilds on CGBJ's code and reports 12 to 15 fps on an RTX 4090; the original repository still does not answer
item.description:
• Vice-Tay's README (08:25 UTC) says the fork now starts from the code PortWatch lists as CGBJ, and on it reports 12 to 15 frames a second indoors and in the yard on an RTX 4090 at 4K on the larger console's profile, with medians of about 13 over sessions of 6 to 8 minutes and longest sessions of 8 to 10 minutes without a crash. Its lanes now read the new base, and it moves to 4th from 7th.
  • The original repository still does not answer. Vice-Tay's README says its author took it down; this page has no statement from that author, GitHub has published no notice naming it and PortWatch still lists it as public. VIctory-7900XTX merged parts of the code at 08:05 UTC, so the work stays in public trees.
  • That gives a second reading of the same code: about 13 on an RTX 4090 at 4K in Vice-Tay's hands and 17 to 18 on an RTX 5090 in its own journal, against the 25 PortWatch relays. Nothing reports a session of 10 minutes or more at 20, so Playable stays at no and the estimate is held.
  • vilocity's latest test run shows a median of about 14 frames a second on its default profile, up from 11.5. five-star-recomp's status page says the city at night is on screen but washes out to white, with a world frame at about 540 milliseconds. News check: XDA has picked up PortWatch's 25 for CGBJ, no new notice names a project on this page, and there is no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two.

item.title: CGBJ's repository stops answering within an hour of going public; the routine review holds the estimate
item.description:
• The repository PortWatch named at 07:23 UTC as the public code of CGBJ answered this page's read at 07:34 UTC and did not answer at 08:01 or 08:03 UTC, while other repositories did: it is missing, private or removed. GitHub has published no notice naming it and the reason is not known. The row keeps its place, 11th, without a link.
  • What was read while it was public stays as the row's reading: a fork of VIctory-7900XTX with six commits on top, medians of about 17 to 18 frames a second in the opening street on an RTX 5090 in its own journal, and no session of play. PortWatch still relays 25 and still lists the code as public.
  • Routine review of the estimate: held at around midnight UTC going into Friday 27 November. For moving earlier: the code was public for a time, PortWatch reversed the lowering that moved the estimate at 05:41 UTC, and VIctory-7900XTX reports about 19 in a city street with patches it is testing. Against: the journal's own figures are under 20, the repository is gone again, PortWatch's figure changed three times in four hours, and nobody reports a session of play with its length.
  • ScarlettPort reports 5.4 frames a second while walking and turning, up from about 4, and moves to 23rd from 28th. five-star-recomp says the world's lit image now reaches the screen, with surfaces still black. Native VIctory for macOS, a port that runs on Metal without Wine and gets past the start screen, joins the watch list.

item.title: CGBJ's code is now public: PortWatch says 25 fps, its own journal 17 to 18; VIctory-7900XTX reports about 19 with new patches
item.description:
• PortWatch said at 07:23 UTC that the build it lists as CGBJ is now public as GPL-3.0 source, and put its figure back to an average of 25 frames a second in gameplay with 8 GB of system memory, after 25 and then 20 earlier today. Its entry still says independent reproduction is needed.
  • This page read the repository over git and now links it. It is a fork of VIctory-7900XTX with six commits of NVIDIA work on top. Its README gives no figures of its own, and its development journal records medians of 54 to 58 milliseconds a frame, about 17 to 18 frames a second, in the opening street on an RTX 5090 with 32 GB of memory around midnight UTC, in harness runs of about two minutes, with a sustained 20 still open then.
  • The row is now read from the project's own documents, as every public row is, with PortWatch's account relayed in its status: speed 17 to 18, a 2-minute run and a picture with open faults. That is 3 steps short and 11th, from 9th. Nothing reports a session of play with its length, so Playable stays at no and the estimate is held; with public code, anyone can now test the build.
  • VIctory-7900XTX rewrote its README at 07:19 UTC: its goal is a stable 30 frames a second or more without ray tracing, and a city street runs at 13 to 17 on its defaults or about 19 with two renderer patches that are off by default. It no longer lists the 41-minute session it reported on 25 November; this page keeps that reading and says so, and it stays first. News check: no new notice and no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two, and a second outlet, TalkEsport, reports the account of an email from Rockstar by the developer of the private build omonkey.

item.title: Hourly check: no session lengths yet and no release of the private build; one more fork on the watch list
item.description:
• Neither PortWatch's entry for the private build CGBJ (20 frames a second, relayed) nor VIctory-NVIDIA's README (20 to 22 on average indoors) has added a session length, and the private build has not been released. Playable stays at no and the estimate is held.
  • Added to the watch list: ShakiraRED(dt), a performance fork of VIctory's code that AnyXboxX credits. On an RTX 4090 its README gives single samples from gameplay scenes, 18 to 20 frames a second in a lighter scene and 13.7 to 15 in a heavier one, with some draws dropped for missing pipelines and no session length. It has had no commits since 25 November.
  • VIctory-forkAMD's notes now report about 8.9 frames a second over a 15-minute run without a crash on a Radeon RX 7600, up from 6.2 to 6.4. VIniVIdiVIci withdrew the 7.3 it published at 05:35 UTC after finding a fault in one switch and gives 6.5 again, with switches that are off by default.
  • News check: the press has not picked up either report of 20 or more and still cites VIctory-7900XTX's 13 to 22 or older figures of 2 to 5. GitHub has published no new notice, and there is no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two since the build leaked beyond the notice against Leonida.

item.title: PortWatch lowers its figure for the private build CGBJ to 20 fps; the estimate moves a quarter of a day later
item.description:
• PortWatch's stand-in editor changed its account of the private build CGBJ at 05:34 UTC: a stable 20 frames a second in gameplay, where it said an average of 25 at 03:58 UTC, with cutscenes at 30, on an NVIDIA card with 16 GB of video memory and 10 GB of system memory. It points to a video and says the build will be released soon, and still gives no session length and no word on whether every frame is rendered. The row reads 20 and stays 9th.
  • The estimate moves a quarter of a day later, to around midnight UTC going into Friday 27 November, as the mark published at 04:04 UTC said it would if PortWatch lowered its account. The promised release is not a mark; a session of 10 minutes or more averaging 20 or more, reported with its length, would bring the estimate forward again.
  • Correction: at 05:17 UTC this page read VIniVIdiVIci's speed lane from a median measured with switches that are off by default, 6.5 frames a second. Figures for a setup a project does not use by default do not count, so the lane reads 6.0 again. Its README now gives 7.3 with eleven such switches on, and its place, 18th, is unchanged.
  • OpenScarlett's README (05:20 UTC) reports a retail title it does not name through its intro video, menus and loading screens at 30 to 60 frames a second on a 4 GB GTX 1650 Ti, with live 3D gameplay as its next step. VIctory-NVIDIA and VIctory-7900XTX have published no new figures.

item.title: No session lengths yet for the two fastest reports; small changes elsewhere
item.description:
• Neither VIctory-NVIDIA nor PortWatch's entry for the private build CGBJ has added a session length in the last hour, so both stay 3 steps short and Playable stays at no. VIctory-NVIDIA has not been updated since 03:41 UTC, and VIctory-7900XTX's README is unchanged.
  • VIniVIdiVIci's README (05:13 UTC) now gives a median of 6.5 frames a second in its first room with a set of switches that are off by default, and ScarlettPort's (05:02 UTC) about 4 while walking and turning on an RTX 3060, with its screen lighting passes fixed. Neither changes step or place.
  • On the watch list, XTP joins: a compatibility layer tested on a Radeon RX 6700 XT whose README says no title is usable yet. The hourly news check found the newest press pieces still putting builds at 2 to 5 frames a second or citing VIctory-7900XTX's 13 to 22, none reporting the 20 or more claimed since last night, no new notice and no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two.

item.title: PortWatch stands by its CGBJ figures; Victory-United nearly doubles in its test room after merging VIctory-7900XTX's speed work
item.description:
• PortWatch's stand-in editor has added that the private build CGBJ averaged 25 frames a second on an NVIDIA card with 16 GB of video memory in a PC with 8 GB of system memory, and calls those figures "not a typo". No session length has been added, so its lanes and its place are unchanged.
  • Victory-United's README (04:41 UTC) reports a 15-minute run at a median of 9.3 frames a second in its test room after merging VIctory-7900XTX's speed work, against 5.0 before. The character still only stands in the room, so it stays at stage 5.
  • PortWatch now gives about 8 frames a second for the gameplay it saw on Belobug's fork, where it said about 4; that fork's README says 5 to 8. VIctory-NVIDIA and VIctory-7900XTX have published nothing new since the last check.

item.title: A public fork, VIctory-NVIDIA, reports 20 to 22 frames a second indoors and joins the table; VItoriaBr moves to 3rd
item.description:
• VIctory-NVIDIA, a fork of VIctory-7900XTX made to run on NVIDIA cards, joins the table at stage 6. Its README has reported since 23:46 UTC on 25 November about 20 to 22 rendered frames a second on average indoors in the opening on an RTX 5070 with a Ryzen 7 9800X3D, and 24 to 31 in lighter places. This page found it only now, through a fork of it that PortWatch's scout listed.
  • The conditions matter: the smaller console's profile, the world drawn at 960 by 540 and upscaled, ray tracing mostly off, and its fastest settings, which leave some stretched bodies and miscoloured skin. One run each in the same PC measured 19.3 on the RTX 5070 and 14.9 on an RTX 5060 Ti, and a fork measured on an RTX 4060 Ti with a Ryzen 5 5600X, now on the watch list as VKarameloVI, reports 7 to 12. Its start script is set up for a driver feature that adds generated frames, and the figures here are its rendered frames.
  • It gives no session length, so it is on the speed step the bar asks for and 3 steps short on stability, in 11th place. It is the first public code to report an average of 20 or more in play, and with PortWatch's report on the private build CGBJ it is the second report of that kind today. The estimate, moved earlier at 04:04 UTC, is held: it already assumed a build near 20.
  • Also: VItoriaBr's README (04:09 UTC) now documents 4 to 6 frames a second on its current settings, where this page read 3.5 to 6 before, so the middle of its range reaches 5 and it moves from 10th to 3rd; its best open-world measurement of 22 comes from an experimental build that is not its default and is not counted. VIniVIdiVIci corrects its figures to a median of 6.0 in its first room, and five-star-recomp's lit world now shows a night sky at about one frame a second. The hourly news check found no press yet on PortWatch's CGBJ report, no new notice and no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two.

item.title: PortWatch reports a private build, CGBJ, at 25 frames a second in gameplay; the estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier
item.description:
• PortWatch's update of 03:58 UTC, made by a stand-in editor, says PortWatch has now seen the private build CGBJ and reports an average of 25 frames a second in gameplay on an NVIDIA card, with interiors and cutscenes near 30 and a picture it rates close to the console with minor glitches. Until now it listed the build at about 4, unlit.
  • What the report does not give: a session length, the test machine beyond the card's maker, or whether every frame is rendered and none generated. The code is private, so nobody outside the group can test it, and PortWatch's own notes say its graphics degraded as speed improved before the rating was raised. This page relays it as unconfirmed.
  • CGBJ's speed lane now reads 25, the first row on the step the playable bar asks for. With no session length it is still 3 steps short and moves from 28th to 8th, and VIctory-7900XTX stays first. Playable stays at no: the bar asks for 30 minutes without a crash at 20 or more, reported.
  • The estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier, to around the evening of Thursday 26 November, UTC, with about 6 in 10 by the end of that day. The published mark asked for a session of 10 minutes or more averaging 20 with its length, which this report does not give, so the move rests on evidence the mark did not foresee and is undone if PortWatch withdraws or lowers the figure.

item.title: VIctory-7900XTX pushes a night of speed work, with its README's figures unchanged
item.description:
• VIctory-7900XTX pushed code for the first time since it was published: merges of speed work made between 00:16 and 01:48 UTC, one of which its notes measure, standing in a street, at a mean of 88.8 milliseconds a frame against 100.5. Its README still gives 13 to 22 frames a second in most scenes and a longest session of 41 minutes, so its lanes are unchanged and it stays first.
  • Kelvaroq's README and its new release notes (03:24 UTC) restate its measurements without change: heavy frames at a mean of 7.6 frames a second in a 300-second run on an RTX 5080, and the outside tester's 36-minute session at 10 on average. Its lanes and its place are unchanged.
  • VIniVIdiVIci's README (03:22 UTC) measures about 6 frames a second in its first room over a scripted 280-second walk, against 4.9 before two changes to its pass over the descriptor heap, and says every session so far ran with a switch that is off by default. It stays on the second speed step, in 16th place.
  • Victory-United's README (03:30 UTC) now says moving the character is not confirmed: a run that held the move keys for about two minutes did not move it, so its figures are for standing in a room. It stays at stage 5.

item.title: Two claims of faster private builds are not counted; BRVIctory-ka1qux reports its ray-traced street at about 3 frames a second
item.description:
• A reader reported on this page's issues that the private build PortWatch lists as NotNozy reached 20 frames a second in some sections of a live stream. PortWatch's own entry gives it no measured frame rate, crash record or test machine and marks it self-reported, so it is not on this page.
  • GameGPU relays a statement, posted on social media by a project it calls Portheon, that a closed build runs at 30 frames a second. The report gives no hardware, session length, footage, code or outside tester, and PortWatch does not list the build, so nothing is counted for it. This page still counts no build as playable, and its warning stands: any download offered as GTA VI for PC is fake.
  • BRVIctory-ka1qux's README (02:56 UTC) reports an open-world street at a median of 3.1 to 3.3 frames a second on a Radeon RX 7800 XT with the game's own ray-traced light on by default, the cost of each draw about a tenth lower than in its last build, and no crash in its last 50 runs of 4 to 25 minutes. Its place is unchanged.
  • Victory-United's README (02:55 UTC) records a paired 6-minute run in which 14 performance changes taken from other projects raised its first room from 4.0 to 5.0 frames a second. The hourly news check found no new notice and no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two beyond the Leonida notice.

item.title: The speed lane now reads a session of play first; Kelvaroq passes AnyXboxX for 2nd
item.description:
• From this check a project's speed is read first from the average it reports over its newest session of play of 10 minutes or more, or its median where it gives no average. A project that reports no such session is still read from the middle of the frame rates it reports in play. Scripted or automated runs and scenes standing still do not count as play.
  • The reason is that low figures were not being read evenly. Since 00:11 UTC a rate given for a condition of play has counted as a row's low end, which was applied to AnyXboxX, VIctory-7900XTX and Flamingo but not to klbf-lab, whose README mentions dips to about 0.5 to 1 frames a second while a new area loads. A session average already includes such dips, and a sustained session is what the playable bar asks about.
  • Kelvaroq is now read from its unnamed tester's 36-minute session, 10 frames a second on average. That is the fourth speed step, so it is 1 step short of the bar and passes AnyXboxX for 2nd. klbf-lab reads 5.2 over its 77 minutes, Vice-Tay 7.0, Flamingo 8.6, Vertex 6.9 and ruff-lab 3.6, each on the same step and in the same place as before.
  • VIctory-7900XTX stays first. It gives no average for its 41-minute session and AnyXboxX's 13-minute runs are automated, so both are still read from their ranges, 5 to 23.8 and 1 to 17. No project's own figures changed in this check and the estimate is unchanged; victory-fork's run notes (02:17 to 02:30 UTC) record two more changes that cut copying or its submission thread's work without shortening the frame, and trace black surfaces in one area to textures the card had no room for.

item.title: Flamingo's low figure is read like the leaders' and it falls to 13th; victory-fork measures a small gain
item.description:
• Flamingo's README has said since 25 November that its first scene falls to about 4 frames a second for a few seconds while turning, as textures stream in. That now counts as the low end of its speed lane, by the rule stated here at 00:11 UTC for AnyXboxX and VIctory-7900XTX: a rate a project gives for a stretch or a condition of play counts. The middle of its range goes from 10.9 to 9, which leaves it 3 steps short of the playable bar and takes it from 5th to 13th. Its own figures have not changed, and how every row's low figures and session averages are read is being reviewed.
  • victory-fork's README (02:15 UTC) measures one new change, a cache for buffer lookups, as saving about 14 milliseconds a frame on its test machine and another change as saving nothing. It says shadowed areas are still black and the graphics device is still lost 30 to 50 minutes into a session, with the PC's memory nearly full at two of the losses and no cause shown.
  • vilocity's README (02:01 UTC) says textures that were waiting for card memory now load, among them a print on one character's clothing and faces in the opening cutscenes, at the same 11 frames a second. Its runs still end at about 7 minutes.
  • Take-Two's notice against Leonida is now widely reported: TweakTown, Decrypt and heise are among those covering the 3,007 repositories GitHub removed, and KitGuru reports notices against repositories and chat servers without naming any. None of the reports read names another project as a target, GitHub has published no new notice, and neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has commented since the build leaked beyond that notice.

item.title: Victory-United joins the table with a 35-minute scripted run; vilocity clears its slow launches
item.description:
• Victory-United's README (01:37 UTC) reports one 35-minute run without a crash on an RTX 3080 Ti, with 31 minutes in the first room at a median of 4.8 frames a second, at half render scale on the smaller console's profile. A script reached the room and the character stood still, so it leaves the watch list for the table at stage 5, first in that group.
  • vilocity's README (01:46 UTC) says about half its launches fell into a slow mode of 3 to 5 frames a second, caused by the game's own memory defragmenter on the card and now cleared: four launches in a row ran fast, and its latest run shows a median frame of 86 milliseconds, about 11.6 frames a second. Its runs still end at about 7 minutes.
  • VIctory-7900XTX had its first commit since 22:14 UTC on 25 November, a credit line, and its figures are unchanged. An open pull request on victory-fork describes a 30-minute session on an RTX 5060 Ti at a median of 3.2 frames a second with no loss of the graphics device.

item.title: A launcher project that reuses this page's top ten reports its own test runs; CCS03 joins the watch list
item.description:
• A third-party launcher project now lists this page's top ten and reports its own runs of them on one PC with an RTX 4060 and 8 GB. None is verified: about 14 frames a second over 10 minutes from an earlier AnyXboxX build, about 15 past the intro from VIctory-7900XTX before it ran out of graphics memory, and about 20 on average from Flamingo's newest build with models very dark and the picture flashing. It gives no session length for the last, so no published mark is met.
  • This page is not affiliated with that project or with any site or tool that reuses its standings, does not link to it and does not vouch for it. The lanes still read each project's own report.
  • CCS03, a fork of victory-fork tested on a laptop RTX 4060 with 8 GB, joins the watch list: play under control at 3 to 7.8 frames a second in runs of up to 31 minutes.
  • Otherwise quiet: victory-fork's newest runs measured no gain from one change to its heap pass, and GitHub has published no new notice.

item.title: The press picks up VIctory-7900XTX; Kelvaroq says a memory layer in testing cuts its copying by more than nine tenths
item.description:
• PC Gamer's running explainer now notes the claim of 16 frames a second on average for the fork PortWatch lists first, and adds that clips of such builds are hard to verify. VGTimes has reported VIctory-7900XTX's 13 to 22 frames a second and its 41-minute session from its README. Neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has commented beyond the Leonida notice.
  • Kelvaroq's README (00:55 UTC) says a new memory layer, still in testing, cut the memory copied each frame from over 100 MB to under 8 MB in its first scenes. It gives no frame rate for it and says nothing will be published until it is validated across the whole game, so its figures and its lanes are unchanged.
  • victory-fork's run notes (01:11 UTC) record a fifth loss of the graphics device, about 41 minutes into a session, in the same part of the story as the three before it.
  • On the watch list, victory-nvidia-8gb joins: the fork of victory-fork that Vertex builds on, reporting 8 to 10 frames a second on a laptop RTX 4060 with 8 GB.

item.title: vilocity reaches about 11 frames a second on the smaller console's profile; victory-fork loses its graphics device a fourth time at the same place
item.description:
• vilocity's README (00:19 UTC) says it now shows the game the smaller console's profile by default and runs at about 11 frames a second on an RTX 5080, against about 3 on the larger profile: the game then draws fewer pixels and leaves out the ray-traced and hair passes the layer cannot run. Its runs still end at about 7 minutes, so it is still four steps short of the playable bar.
  • victory-fork's README (00:09 UTC) records a fourth loss of the graphics device, 38 minutes in. Three of its four long sessions ended on the way to the same place in the story, so it now ties the fault to what is drawn there and not to the time played. Its headline range is now 7 to 12 frames a second.
  • VIniVIdiVIci's README (00:24 UTC) reports 46 minutes without a crash on an RTX 4060 Ti, 38 of them in the world at 3.75 frames a second overall, and says the world is not shown to have been on screen throughout. It moves from 19th to 16th.
  • The estimate was reviewed and holds at about a day. News check: no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two beyond the Leonida notice, and no new notice names a project on this page.

item.title: AnyXboxX reports dips to 1 to 6 frames a second while the world streams, and VIctory-7900XTX is first again
item.description:
• AnyXboxX's README (23:53 UTC) keeps its default at about 14 to 17 frames a second, a median of 13.7 over 7 minutes, and now names its limits: a 32 GB machine is short of memory and a 12 GB card runs out of texture room, which brings dips to 1 to 6 while the world streams. A mode that favours the picture runs at about 7 to 9.
  • With that low end the middle of the range AnyXboxX reports falls to 9, two steps short of the playable bar. VIctory-7900XTX, one step short, is first again. The two have traded first place twice since 22:39 UTC on small changes in what each reports, and a low figure is read the same way for both: a rate a project gives for a stretch or a condition of play counts, single frames do not.
  • victory-fork's README (23:51 UTC) lists new changes that are written but not yet measured in a game, one of them ported by hand from VIctory-7900XTX, and says video memory has been ruled out as the cause of its lost graphics device.
  • On the watch list, Victory-United now reports 4.9 to 5.2 frames a second in the first room on an RTX 3080 Ti with a longest run of 8 minutes, and ScarlettCompat joins: a layer written from scratch that reports no game frame yet.

item.title: VIctory says only the frame rate keeps the game from working; Sixth Star joins the watch list
item.description:
• VIctory's README (23:27 UTC) now heads its status with the frame rate as the one thing left: about 1 frame a second in the world on a Radeon RX 6700 XT, with the intro cutscene playing and the opening mission reached with the graphics fully displayed. Its figures and its place are unchanged; the faster figures on this page come from forks of its code.
  • Sixth Star, a compatibility layer built from VIctory's code, joins the watch list at its maintainer's request. Its status file reports gameplay at about 5 frames a second on an RTX 3070 as its user's approximate observation, with stability not measured.

item.title: victory-fork now plays at 9 to 12 frames a second in light scenes, for half an hour at a time; VItoriaBr reports a process up for over two hours
item.description:
• victory-fork's README (23:18 UTC) now heads its status with play for half an hour at a time, slowly: about 9 to 12 frames a second in rooms and light outdoor views and 5 to 6 in heavy outdoor views. Its tester played from the opening past the first boat mission, and the graphics device was then lost in sessions of 6, 49 and 31 minutes, cause not known. This is the code most builds share.
  • Its place is unchanged at 6th, two steps short: this page's playable bar asks for 20 frames a second. The README says the thread that prepares submissions is the limit, at about 70 milliseconds a frame plus 13 for every 1,000 draws.
  • VItoriaBr's README gives one measured example of its process staying up for 2 hours 12 minutes, without saying what was played in that time. Read as its longest session, that lifts it from 22nd to 10th.
  • News check: press coverage is still of Take-Two's notice against Leonida, there is no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two beyond that notice, and GitHub's list has no new notice naming a project here. keylime's repository still does not answer.

item.title: AnyXboxX gives a session length and edges back to first; victory-fork reports 49 minutes of play; keylime's repository stops answering
item.description:
• AnyXboxX's README (22:54 UTC) now gives a length for its figure: automated 13-minute runs on an RTX 4070 SUPER at a median of 13.8 frames a second in the world, 15.6 to 17 over the last minute, without a crash, up from 10.9 with its earlier settings. That puts the middle of its reported range just above VIctory-7900XTX's, so the two swap places, each one step short of the playable bar.
  • victory-fork's README (22:50 UTC) reports a 49-minute play session that ended when the graphics device was lost, and a later run it calls the best so far, with the water right and boats floating. It measured that nearly all of the memory it copies back from the card is read by nothing, and names that as the next thing to cut.
  • keylime's repository stopped answering between 22:28 and 22:59 UTC: missing, private or removed. No takedown notice names it and the reason is not known. GitHub's notice list gained one entry, about an unrelated library.
  • klbf-lab removed the names of the game, its characters and its missions from its README. vilocity reports faces lit in the opening cutscenes and a median frame of 222 milliseconds in its latest run. The estimate is unchanged: neither published mark is met.

item.title: VIctory-7900XTX is published with 13 to 22 frames a second in most scenes and goes first; the estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier
item.description:
• VIctory-7900XTX, a fork of VIctory whose README went up at 22:14 UTC, reports 13 to 20 frames a second indoors in the opening, 19 to 22 on the first boat mission and 6 to 10 in a busy street chase on a Radeon RX 7900 XTX at 1440p, with a longest session of 41 minutes without a crash. It gives no average for a whole session and lists flicker on trees and far buildings. PortWatch's owner says it verified the build at about 16 on average; it is one machine and nobody else has reproduced it.
  • It enters at stage 6 in first place, one step short of the playable bar, ahead of AnyXboxX on the middle of its reported range. The estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier, to around midnight UTC going into Friday 27 November, on the mark published at 21:26 UTC, with the caveats set out in the revision note.
  • A reader posted a 12-minute run of AnyXboxX on an RTX 4090 to this page's issues: a median of 2 frames a second in the world, rising to about 7 in its last two minutes, against the README's 12.5 on another card. The page has not verified it. AnyXboxX's speed is now marked unconfirmed, and its place still follows its own report.
  • Vertex, a fork of VIctory measured on an RTX 5070 with 12 GB, joins at stage 6 at its maintainer's request: a median of 6.4 to 9.9 frames a second by run and a longest session of 25 minutes. Victory-United, a tree that gathers pull requests from the forks, joins the watch list.

item.title: VIctory merges about 70 pull requests into its main branch, vilocity clears its last orange marks and VIniVIdiVIci confirms control
item.description:
• VIctory's main branch took 74 commits between 21:35 and 21:57 UTC, its first since 16:51 UTC, among them the drawing of the interface planes the game uses on the smaller console's profile. Its README's status is unchanged at about 1 frame a second.
  • vilocity's README (21:46 UTC) says the last orange marks are gone, with window light and shadows now falling on heads. Its latest test run shows a median frame of 339 milliseconds, about 3 frames a second, where earlier runs showed about 130.
  • VIniVIdiVIci's README (21:48 UTC) says player control is confirmed with scripted input and nobody at the keyboard: the camera turned, the character moved and the pause menu opened.
  • AnyXboxX has not yet given a session length for its figure of about 12 frames a second.

item.title: Vice-Tay reports a 30-minute session at a median of 7 frames a second and moves up to 6th
item.description:
• Vice-Tay's README (21:32 UTC) reports 30 minutes 12 seconds in the world without a crash on an RTX 4090, from a save in the opening mission with the player walking and turning the camera throughout. The median over the session was 7.0 frames a second, 6.3 to 9.5 by stretch and 1.9 to 3.8 through one scene change. Its maintainer ended it by choice because memory grows by about 1 GB a minute. The row moves from 17th to 6th.
  • VIctory's main branch took its first commits since 16:51 UTC: five merges between 21:35 and 21:40 UTC. Its README still gives about 1 frame a second.
  • victory-fork's README (21:28 UTC) says that with its new water read-back a tester's run got past a point where a mission had failed at once, then lost the graphics card for a reason not known. BRVIctory-ka1qux now gives about 3 frames a second on its street with ray-traced light and no longer lists the 6.6 to 6.9 it had reported from an earlier build.

item.title: AnyXboxX reports about 12 frames a second on a new base and takes first place, and the estimate moves to early Friday
item.description:
• AnyXboxX's README (20:50 UTC) says its maintainer measured a median of 12.5 frames a second in the world on an RTX 4070 SUPER at 4K output, about 15 over the last minute with peaks at 30 and no crash, after moving its code to a base it calls Neptune: a packaged edition of VIctory, shipped with its source, whose author it says has no public contact. Its previous base ran at about 5 there. The README does not say how long the session ran, and the figures are its own, from one machine.
  • By the rule AnyXboxX is now first, 1 step short of the playable bar. Its speed lane reads the new base; its stability lane is still a contributor's relayed 45 minutes on the earlier base, and the row says so. Kelvaroq is second.
  • Kelvaroq's README now cites its place on this page and carries a banner for the AI product it is built with. The tester behind its 36-minute session is not named, nobody else has confirmed the session, and PortWatch does not track Kelvaroq as a separate effort because it reads its results as VIctory's and victory-fork's code. A place here is computed from what a project reports about itself and is not a verification; the Positions note now says so.
  • The estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier, to early on Friday 27 November: three reports this evening put play at 10 frames a second or more, though none meets the published mark to the letter, and new marks are in the revision note. A news sweep at 21:21 UTC found nothing new from Rockstar or Take-Two and no notice naming another project. victory-fork's README (21:09 UTC) reports a small gain, a first-room frame down from about 115 to 110 milliseconds.

item.title: Kelvaroq takes first place: an outside tester's 36 minutes at about 10 frames a second on an RTX 4090
item.description:
• Kelvaroq's README (20:53 UTC) records an outside tester's session of 36 minutes 46 seconds without a crash on an RTX 4090, through the opening mission and the next. It averaged 10 frames a second over the whole session and 10.9 after the first ten minutes, which the README describes as loading with dips to 1. It is one session, and the README says its monitor was restarted once.
  • That gives Kelvaroq a session length where it had only 5-minute runs. It is now 2 steps short of the playable bar and takes first place from klbf-lab by the rule: the same picture step and a higher frame rate. It is the best average yet from a session of 20 minutes or more, and the first of Kelvaroq's figures from a second machine.
  • The estimate is unchanged for now. This is the session averaging 10 or more that the published mark for moving later asked for by 12:00 UTC on 26 November, so that mark no longer applies. The mark for moving earlier asks for 12, and playable needs 20.
  • Belobug's fork now reports 5 to 8 frames a second, with 7.2 to 7.7 standing still, and a stand-in light that follows the game's sky. Vice-Tay's README says its current build, rebuilt on VIctory's code, ran the opening cutscene at a median of 0.8 frames a second, and that its 4.3 to 7.5 came from an earlier revision.

item.title: victory-unified reports 58 minutes without a crash, and PortWatch says the private stream build runs on VIctory's code
item.description:
• victory-unified's README (20:38 UTC) reports about 58 minutes in one session with no crash on an RTX 3070 with 8 GB, from the opening into a later mission outdoors, at 2 to 3 frames a second. It follows a fix for the graphics-device failure that ended its two earlier sessions at about 49 minutes.
  • PortWatch added at 20:30 UTC, on its owner's word, that darkworldhm builds on a fork of VIctory, which one is not known. The build is still self-reported and its figures are still a reading of a live stream; its row here says so.
  • VIniVIdiVIci reports four sessions of ten minutes that ran to their time limit without a crash with a texture change for 8 GB cards. There is no commit at victory-fork since 19:39 UTC or on VIctory's main branch since 16:51 UTC, and victory-perf's repository still does not answer.

item.title: darkworldhm, the private build PortWatch saw at up to 24 frames a second, gets a row marked unconfirmed
item.description:
• PortWatch's entry for darkworldhm stood for a round and was raised at 19:59 UTC: its owner now reports free roam at 5 to 24 frames a second on the stream, about 12 to 15 by the owner's reading. The build joins the table as a private row in 11th place with every figure marked as relayed. PortWatch lists it as self-reported, the code is not public, no session length is given, and nothing says whether the counter shows rendered frames. PortWatch's pinned notes since then ask the streamer to release the code.
  • A news sweep at 20:16 UTC found no second source for that build. Coverage is still of Take-Two's notice against Leonida, no notice names another project, and there is no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two since the build leaked. A small Manifold market, with four traders, gives about 1 in 5 that GitHub publishes a Take-Two notice naming VIctory by the end of the year.
  • Vice-Tay's maintainer confirmed the move from victory-windows in a request on this page's repository and says the length of its test sessions is unknown. victory-perf's repository still does not answer.
  • The estimate is unchanged. A reading of a stream is not the measured session of 10 minutes or more, averaging 12 or more in rendered frames, that the published mark asks for.

item.title: PortWatch now reports a private build at about 12 frames a second in free roam, ruff-lab reaches stage 6, and the estimate is held
item.description:
• PortWatch replaced its pinned note at 19:42 UTC: its owner now reports a private build, darkworldhm, shown on a live stream in free roam at 5 to 18 frames a second, about 12 to 15 by the owner's reading, reportedly on an RTX 50-series card. PortWatch lists it as self-reported, its code is not public, what it builds on is not known, and nothing says whether the figure counts rendered frames only. This page waits one round, or for a second source, before giving a private build a row.
  • ruff-lab moves to stage 6: its README now reports the player in control with a DualShock 4 on a Radeon RX 6600 XT with 8 GB, 16 GB of memory and a hard disk, in a 39-minute session without a crash at 3.6 frames a second on average.
  • victory-fork's README (19:39 UTC) now heads its status with 8 to 10 frames a second in the first rooms and 5 to 8.5 through the opening cutscene, measured with changes that are off by default, and its evening code is in the tree with no speed gain shown. victory-windows is now published as Vice-Tay by the same maintainer, and victory-perf's repository still does not answer.
  • Estimate reviewed this round and held at midday on Friday 27 November. The stream figure is one viewer's reading with no session length and no word on frame generation, so the published mark for moving earlier is not met. Against it, three builds of victory-fork's code became unavailable today with no notice published, and victory-fork reports no new speed. A measured session of 10 minutes or more averaging 12 or more, rendered frames only, would move the estimate a quarter of a day earlier.

item.title: victory-fork reports no new speed but fewer long frames in a test, and victory-perf's repository stops answering
item.description:
• victory-fork's README (19:21 UTC) claims no frame-rate gain and says its headline figures stand. A frame capture now built into the layer puts the card's time for the game's own commands at 15 to 25 milliseconds a frame in the opening cutscene, far less than a whole frame, and the project says the time taken by the layer's own work does not add up yet.
  • Keeping part of the game's memory copies on the graphics card cut the time spent in frames longer than 250 milliseconds from 21 and 26% to 4 and 6% in the opening cutscene, in two launches each way. The project calls it a result, not yet a default, and reports two other changes that measured no gain and were dropped.
  • It also says a review of the open pull requests for frame rate found no single large gain, and that the change it had listed as the large step would be a modest one on its test PC.
  • victory-perf's repository stopped answering over git between 18:56 and 19:28 UTC: missing, private or removed, with no published takedown notice naming it and the reason not known. It is the third build of victory-fork's code to become unavailable today, after ztrx and the private build omonkey, and a news sweep at 19:27 UTC found no report about it. Two more forks join the watch list: VIctory-forkAMD and HybridGt.

item.title: PortWatch says it has found no build above 10 frames a second in free roam, two forks report longer sessions and victory-windows joins the table
item.description:
• PortWatch's owner pinned a note at 18:57 UTC saying it has found no evidence of any build above 10 frames a second in free roam, and that claims of more should be doubted. The higher figures on this page, on Flamingo's and victory-perf's rows, are those projects' own from one machine each and stay marked unconfirmed.
  • VIniVIdiVIci's README (18:46 UTC) now gives 3 to 5 frames a second by scene, with 3.2 measured under player control, and a 15-minute session that ran to its time limit without a crash. A 30-minute session also reached its limit, but the project does not count it because its shutdown was not recorded cleanly.
  • victory-unified reports a second session of about 49 minutes, this one on its current build, ended like the first by a graphics-device failure, and says it has changed settings to prevent it.
  • New row at stage 6: victory-windows, a fork of VIctory whose README reports the controllable first room at 4.3 to 7.5 frames a second on an RTX 4090, with no run length stated and no commit since 09:15 UTC. The card filter now offers Intel, for the three lower-stage projects that list test reports from Intel cards.

item.title: PortWatch reports the private build omonkey taken down, hours after its developer's reported letter from Rockstar
item.description:
• PortWatch removed omonkey from its board at 18:19 UTC, saying on its owner's word that the private build has been taken down. Its code was never public, so there is nothing to check, and no notice or statement has been published. VGTimes reported earlier today that its developer reported receiving a letter from Rockstar and stopped streaming. Its row here keeps its last reported status.
  • With ztrx's repository and account gone since about 17:00 UTC, two builds of victory-fork's code have gone dark today with no reason published. The mark published with the estimate asks for a takedown notice that names VIctory, victory-fork or a build of it, and GitHub's list holds none, so the estimate is unchanged. Both cases will weigh in its next review.
  • vilocity's README now gives 4 to 8 frames a second in the first room on an RTX 5080, up from 3 to 7. klbf-lab's README adds that it never publishes a build that crashed in its own tests and that its 77-minute session was stopped by choice. XCL merged 28 pull requests into its main branch with its status row unchanged.

item.title: VI-BR-PORT joins the table near the top, and ruff-lab logs 21.8 minutes without player control
item.description:
• VI-BR-PORT, a fork of victory-fork for NVIDIA cards with 8 GB, joins at stage 6. Its README, in Portuguese, reports control, the HUD and the pause menu working at 4 to 7 frames a second at 1080p on an RTX 4060 Ti, sessions of an hour without losing the graphics device, and all 25,758 of the game's shaders translating on that card, with everything in shadow black. These are its own figures and estimates from one machine. The length of those sessions places it 4th, 2 steps short of the playable bar.
  • ruff-lab's results log now holds a session of 21.8 minutes without a crash at 3.23 frames a second on average on an 8 GB Radeon RX 6600 XT with a hard disk. It says player movement does not work yet because of a controller input problem, so it stays at stage 5.
  • vilocity's README says its rainbow glitter is gone and every shader now translates, still at 3 to 7 frames a second. five-star-recomp's status page says boots now stay 5 to 7 minutes in the world, with the lit picture still wrong.
  • News check: other trackers repeat that ztrx's repository and account are gone, and none gives a reason. GitHub's list holds no new notice, and neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has commented since the build leaked.

item.title: victory-fork measures 4.5 frames a second in a play session, and the estimate moves back to under two days
item.description:
• victory-fork's README (17:28 UTC) reports a 370-second play session at 4.5 frames a second on average, against 10.3 standing still. Half the time goes to frames of about 490 milliseconds in which the card sits idle, because the game maps every streamed texture page itself, about 850 pages in a frame that streams. Two attempts to cut that cost were taken back out, one after faces came out black or red. Its speed lane now reads from its two play sessions, 4.5 on its own RTX 4070 and 7.6 on an RTX 4090 in a pull request, and it stays 3rd.
  • The estimate moves back by three quarters of a day, to midday on Fri 27 Nov. The best averages from sessions of play are 7.6 to 8.6 against the 20 the bar asks for, and the figures of 10 or more came from the lightest scenes. This replaces the check published for 22:00 UTC, and the estimate's note gives the next marks.
  • PortWatch reported at 17:26 UTC that ztrx's repository and the account that published it are both gone, with no takedown notice published. This page has had no answer from the repository since 16:57 UTC, and the reason is still not known.
  • VIniVIdiVIci moves to stage 6: its README reports the player in control on an RTX 4060 Ti at about 2 to 5 frames a second, with a 13-minute session and a dark picture. ruff-lab, asked for in issue 16 on this page's repository, joins at stage 5 with the world drawn at 3.2 to 3.6 frames a second on an 8 GB Radeon RX 6600 XT and no report of control yet. Scarlight now presents itself as a Steam compatibility tool for Linux, at 0.1 to 3 frames a second.

item.title: ztrx's repository stops answering, Belobug's fork reaches 5 to 7 frames a second, and the estimate is reviewed and held
item.description:
• ztrx's repository has not answered since 16:57 UTC, in three checks over 25 minutes while every other tracked repository answered, the last of them after GitHub closed its incident at 16:52 UTC. GitHub's published list holds no notice that names it and PortWatch still lists it, so the reason is not known: a repository made private, deleted or disabled looks the same from outside. Its row keeps its last reported status, without a link.
  • Belobug's fork now reports 5 to 7 frames a second on a Radeon RX 9070 XT, from 3 to 5: 5.4 to 6.7 standing still in a scene of 8,400 draws, less while driving. Its README puts the gain down to letting the game's submissions return before the card is done and to using game memory in place instead of copying it. Its speed lane moves to step 3 and it rises to 4th.
  • BRVIctory-ka1qux has turned the game's own ray-traced light on by default, the first public build on this page to do so. Its README says it costs 0.05 to 0.1 seconds a frame and has been checked on one open-world street only, in four runs of 5 to 11 minutes without a crash.
  • The estimate was reviewed at 17:24 UTC and held at about a day. For it: three code bases now report about 10 frames a second in early scenes, more builds and machines report every hour, and VIctory's own README says you can get into the game. Against it: those figures are best cases, victory-fork's maintainer says the fork's own are for a scene standing still and that the game's translated shaders now cost more than the layer, and no long session has averaged 10. The check published for about 22:00 UTC stands, and without a report of 15 in play or of 10 outside the first interiors from a long run by then the estimate moves a quarter of a day later. Neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has commented since the build leaked.

item.title: VIctory's own README now says you can get into the game, and victory-fork qualifies its 10 frames a second
item.description:
• VIctory's README (16:51 UTC) now opens with "Not playable yet, but you can get into the game". It says the intro cutscene plays and the opening mission is reached with the graphics fully displayed at about 1 frame a second on a Radeon RX 6700 XT: textured and lit, without ray-traced shadows or indirect light. Its picture lane moves from step 1 to step 2.
  • victory-fork's maintainer added a limit at 16:54 UTC to the figures reported here at 15:38 and 16:19 UTC: the 9.6 and 10.3 frames a second are for the scene standing still. While the camera moves the game streams assets, and about half the time goes to frames of about 490 milliseconds in which the card sits idle for about 330. The README did not say so when this page's last entry was written. Its speed lane now reads 2 to 12, and the estimate is unchanged ahead of its next routine review.
  • BRVIctory-ka1qux's README says the game's own ray-traced light now runs as an option on a Radeon RX 7800 XT: shaded buildings, trees and characters get bounced light, at about 0.05 seconds more per frame, in three runs of 5, 6 and 11 minutes without a crash. It is the third public code base to report this, after DexNom Runtime and a pull request to victory-fork, and it stays off by default.
  • Kelvaroq's README now says control of the character, the HUD and pausing are verified in play, and that heavy frames are down to 108.5 milliseconds. GitHub's incident was still open at 16:57 UTC, with Pages at partial outage, so this page may update late.

item.title: victory-fork passes 10 frames a second in its first rooms, and two more builds join the table
item.description:
• victory-fork's README (16:19 UTC) puts its first rooms at 97 milliseconds a frame, 10.3 frames a second, with three changes that are off by default. It also adds up the card's time: about 50 of 87 busy milliseconds are the game's own passes as translated, so with every pass of the layer's own removed the scene would still run at only about 20, and the translated shaders have to get cheaper too. The figure is from the first rooms, so neither mark published with the estimate is met and the estimate stays where it is.
  • Two builds join at stage 6, each on its own figures from one machine. Kelvaroq, from the account that published Palmwave, says the opening mission is playable at about 10 rendered frames a second in typical views and 7 to 8 in its heaviest scenes at 4K output on an RTX 5080, in measured runs of 5 minutes. victory-unified, which combines four forks' work, reports about 2 frames a second on an RTX 3070 with 8 GB and one session of 49 minutes 42 seconds, and that session length places it 3 steps short of the playable bar.
  • vilocity's README now gives 3 to 7 frames a second in the first room on an RTX 5080, up from 2 to 5, after leaving out the denoisers of ray-tracing passes it does not run. Its speed lane moves to step 3 and it passes BRVIctory-ka1qux.
  • TechRadar reported on 25 November that some builds have the opening chapter playable at a few frames a second, which is far from this page's bar. No statement from Rockstar or Take-Two has appeared since the build leaked. GitHub's status page has shown an incident since 15:55 UTC that affects Pages and Git operations, and two of this page's deployments have failed, so updates may arrive late.

item.title: victory-fork measures 9.6 frames a second in its first rooms, VIctory's main branch moves again, and two builds join the table
item.description:
• victory-fork's README (15:38 UTC) puts its first rooms at 104 milliseconds a frame, 9.6 frames a second, with two changes that are off by default, from about 120 that morning. It says the layer's submit thread and the card are both full, so taking time off one alone moved the frame by 0 to 7 percent, and that the console's pace of 33 milliseconds is still far off. The figure is under both marks published with the estimate, which stays where it is.
  • VIctory's maintainer pushed 82 commits to its main branch at 15:46 UTC, the first since 01:36 UTC: texture uploads made in batches and only when their bytes change, cheaper memory tracking and shader fixes. Its README still gives the world at 1 to 2 seconds a frame.
  • Two builds join at stage 6. CBL VIctory, asked for in issue 14 on this page's repository, reports a run of 27 minutes 38 seconds on an RTX 5080 at 3.6 to 6.4 frames a second by scene, ended by hand, after an earlier run crashed at 20 minutes: its own figures from one machine, and it enters 3 steps short of the playable bar. Doomsday is a private build that PortWatch says it verified with ray-traced lighting at about 3 to 5 frames a second and almost no crashes. That is PortWatch's account, not the group's own, and the code is not public.
  • VItoriaBr's README now says skin, terrain, foliage and shadows are working under a shaded stand-in for ambient light taken from Belobug's fork, at up to 6 frames a second on an RTX 5060 Ti. Its picture lane moves from step 2 to step 4 on that claim.

item.title: The standings can be filtered by system, card maker and lane
item.description:
• Each row now says which systems and graphics card makers the project or its testers report running it on. It may run on others.
  • A "Filter the table" link above the standings narrows the rows by system, by card maker and by a minimum on each lane, for example a session of 30 minutes or more. Positions keep their numbers when rows are hidden. A reader suggested both in issues 12 and 13 on this page's repository.

item.title: A private build's developer reports a letter from Rockstar, and Flamingo logs a 24-minute session at 8.6 frames a second
item.description:
• VGTimes reports that the developer of the private build listed here as omonkey reports receiving a letter from Rockstar and has stopped streaming the work, while promising further updates. The letter has not been published and Rockstar has not commented. It is the first report of this kind seen here.
  • Flamingo's run log reports a 24-minute play session through the whole opening and on into the city, at 8.6 frames a second on average in the world on an RTX 4070. That is the highest average reported from a session of 20 minutes or more, from one machine and unconfirmed, and it is under the 10 the next mark asks for.
  • An open pull request against victory-fork reports the game's ray-tracing structure builder running whole through 7 minutes of play, kept off by default because it costs about 88 milliseconds a frame. VIniVIdiVIci moves from the watch list into the table at stage 5: its README reports the world at 3 to 5 frames a second on an RTX 4060 Ti, with no input tested yet.
  • Forecast review: the estimate stays at the evening of Thu 26 Nov. The afternoon has brought more builds, a session from a new game into the open world and ray tracing as an experiment, but no figure above 14 in play, and victory-fork's main code has not moved since 12:43 UTC. News check: no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two, and no notice naming another project.

item.title: DexNom Runtime runs the game's ray tracing as an experiment, and klbf-lab reaches the open world from a new game
item.description:
• DexNom Runtime's test report (14:52 UTC) says that with an experimental mode on, the game builds and walks its ray-tracing structures in the outdoor city on a Radeon RX 7900 XTX at about 1 frame a second, and that the lighting on individual objects is not yet verified. PortWatch says it saw ray-traced lighting working in the build, and moved it to first place on its own board at 14:56 UTC.
  • klbf-lab's README (14:55 UTC) reports play from a new game to the open world on its own saves: the first two missions, then free roam at about 5 to 8 frames a second while driving and walking, in the 77-minute session it reported earlier. It stays first here.
  • vilocity moves from the watch list into the table at stage 6: its README says the opening cutscenes and the first room play at 2 to 5 frames a second on an RTX 5080, with a driver timeout about 7 minutes in. AnyXboxX reports a 23-minute run without a crash on Linux on a Radeon RX 9070 XT, past the opening mission at a median of 3.7.
  • The estimate is unchanged. Ray tracing at 1 frame a second does not bring the 20 the bar asks for closer, and no report yet reaches 15 in play or 10 outside the first interiors. victory-fork's main code has not moved since 12:43 UTC.

item.title: DexNom Runtime joins the table after PortWatch ranks it second on its own board
item.description:
• PortWatch added DexNom Runtime, a fork of VIctory for AMD Radeon cards, to its board in second place at 14:34 UTC. It says it has seen the build running level with Belobug's: the open world close to the retail game, played through missions at about 3 to 4 frames a second.
  • The fork's own test report gives 3.5 to 4 frames a second indoors on a Radeon RX 7900 XTX from a saved game, with interior lighting still wrong and no session length. On this page's rule it enters at stage 6, 6 steps short of the playable bar.
  • five-star-recomp's status page says a boot ran 18 minutes in the world without losing the graphics device, once it held back the game's ray-tracing passes. Its picture of the world is still in red only.
  • VIctory-macOS reports frames in the world on an M5 Pro down from 4.5 seconds to about 2.4 to 2.9. victory-fork's main code has not moved since 12:43 UTC, and the estimate is unchanged.

item.title: VIctory-Belobug-AMD shades its stand-in light, and IGN asks Take-Two for comment
item.description:
• VIctory-Belobug-AMD's README (14:00 UTC) says its stand-in for ray-traced light is now weaker in creases and under objects, and that the game's own sun and lamp shadows work. It still reports 3 to 5 frames a second on a Radeon RX 9070 XT, says about 380 draws a frame are dropped, and says the frame is bound by the processor's work.
  • VIctory-macOS reports its current code staying in the world for over 20 minutes without freezing on an M3 Max, at 0.1 to 0.2 frames a second. Nobody has reached gameplay on a Mac.
  • News check: IGN has reported on the takedown and says it has asked Take-Two for comment. No statement from Rockstar or Take-Two has appeared since the build leaked, and GitHub's list shows no notice naming another project.
  • VIniVIdiVIci, a fork of victory-fork checked on an RTX 4060 Ti, joins the watch list at a reader's request. Its README says it has not yet published results of its own in play. The estimate is unchanged at the evening of Thu 26 Nov.

item.title: klbf-lab plays the second mission to its end, two forks join the table, and the estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier
item.description:
• klbf-lab's README (13:47 UTC) reports the opening mission and all of the second played to the end in one 77-minute session without a crash on its newest test build, on a Radeon RX 9070 XT, at about 5.2 frames a second on average and about 9 in flight. It says the game's own saves work, and that vegetation turns magenta and the ground stays very dark at night.
  • Two forks of victory-fork join the table at stage 6, on their READMEs' own figures from one machine each. Flamingo reports the first gameplay scene of a title it does not name at 9 to 12 frames a second on an RTX 4070 at reduced resolution, about 14 in its lightest view, in 15-minute runs, and enters second in the order. BRVIctory-ka1qux reports a 25-minute play session and 6.6 to 6.9 in steady open-world views on a Radeon RX 7800 XT.
  • The estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier, to the evening of Thu 26 Nov, just over a day away. Flamingo's is the second report of 10 or more in play, from a second machine after victory-perf's, which is the condition this page published at 10:36 UTC. Both come from the lightest scenes, Flamingo's newest code is at 9 to 10, and ordinary play elsewhere is 5 to 9 against the 20 the bar asks for, so the move is small.
  • What moves it next. Earlier by a quarter of a day: 15 or more in play on any machine, or 10 or more outside the first interiors from a long run. Later by a quarter of a day: these figures withdrawn or contradicted, a takedown notice naming VIctory, victory-fork or a build of it, or neither of the earlier marks reported by the review at about 22:00 UTC on 25 November.

item.title: klbf-lab's test build gets through the seaplane flight, and a second card confirms its water fix
item.description:
• klbf-lab's README (13:12 UTC) says that on its newest test build the boat, a seaplane take-off, the flight at about 9 frames a second and the water landing in the second mission all work on a Radeon RX 9070 XT. It has not yet played that mission to its end on the build.
  • It says another user confirmed the water fix on an RTX 5070 Ti, in a build of that user's own. klbf-lab stays first in the stage 6 order, 2 steps short of the playable bar.
  • victory-fork's main code has not moved since 12:43 UTC. An open pull request reports the game running 74 seconds with the builder of its ray-tracing structures switched on, where it crashed within seconds before; nothing changes on screen yet.
  • VIctory-macOS reports its current code loading into the world on an M5 Pro without freezing, at 0.2 frames a second, up from 0.1. Nobody has reached gameplay on a Mac.

item.title: Stage 6 is now ordered by a published rule, and klbf-lab moves to first
item.description:
• Until now the order inside a stage was this page's own judgement. From this check the 13 rows at stage 6 are ordered by their lanes and nothing else: fewest steps short of the playable bar on speed and stability together, then the better picture, the higher frame rate and the longer session. The key under the standings title states the rule, and each row shows its count.
  • Speed is now read as the middle of the frame rates a project reports in play, where it was the best of them, so a best-case scene no longer sets the step. victory-perf's 4.5 to 14 reads as step 3 of 6, down from 4, and VItoriaBr's 3.5 to 6 as step 2, down from 3.
  • The order today: klbf-lab, victory-fork, AnyXboxX, ztrx, VIctory-Belobug-AMD, victory-perf, omonkey, victory-amd, suri, VItoriaBr, ScarlettPort, CGBJ and VIctory. klbf-lab and victory-fork are level at 2 steps short, and klbf-lab's picture is a step better. A project that reports no run length counts as having none, which is why VItoriaBr and ScarlettPort sit lower than before.
  • The rule reads only what projects report about themselves, on different cards and scenes, and it does not count how far into the story a build has been played. Stages below 6 have no lanes and are still ordered by this page's reading.

item.title: Correction: victory-fork withdraws the 8.9 frames a second reported here, and gives 7 to 8
item.description:
• At 12:20 UTC this page reported victory-fork's first room at 6.0 frames a second by default and 8.9 with a newer draw path. At 12:43 UTC the project withdrew both figures: its README says the two runs stood in different scenes and could not be compared.
  • Its corrected figures come from one run each on an RTX 4070. At the same load a frame takes 145 ms with the newer path off and 124 ms with it on and memory copies made in place, about 6.9 and 8.1 frames a second. On screen it reports 7 to 8 in the first rooms and 10 to 12 in lighter views.
  • The same notes describe a first play session past the first rooms. It reached the open world and lost the graphics device there in about 13 minutes, with the 12 GB card out of room for new textures, and the cause is not known.
  • The estimate does not move: the gain is smaller than first stated, ordinary play is still under 10 frames a second, and nothing was withdrawn as unstable. Also in this check, ScarlettPort reports its frozen overlay fixed, still at about 4 frames a second, and VIctory-macOS reports its loading freezes on Macs fixed.

item.title: Rows at stage 6 now show three lanes: picture, speed and stability
item.description:
• Thirteen projects sit at stage 6, so each of their rows now carries three more meters. Speed is the best average the project reports in play, stability is the longest session it reports without a crash, and picture follows written steps. The key under the standings title lists them, and blue marks the steps that meet the playable bar.
  • On speed, the front of the field is at step 3 of 6, from 5 to 9 frames a second: victory-fork at 8.9, klbf-lab at 8.4 and AnyXboxX at 6.9. victory-perf's unconfirmed 9 to 14 reads as step 4. Playable asks for step 5, 20 frames a second.
  • On stability, klbf-lab and ztrx report sessions of more than an hour, and victory-fork's code and AnyXboxX pass the 30 minutes the bar asks for. On picture, VIctory-Belobug-AMD and one private build read as lit and whole, and most of the others still have black or dark shadows.
  • The lanes were suggested by a reader in issue 8 on this page's repository.

item.title: victory-fork merges a third batch of frame-rate work and measures 8.9 frames a second in its first room
item.description:
• victory-fork's maintainer merged a third batch of frame-rate work at 12:06 UTC. On the maintainer's RTX 4070 the first room averages 6.0 frames a second by default, up from 4.5 to 5 two hours earlier, and 8.9 with a newer draw path switched on, from one run each. The opening cutscene went from 3.1 to 4.2.
  • The notes say that draw path stays off by default: of eight runs with it on, one lost the graphics device 44 seconds into the world for a reason not yet found. They also say the regular dips in earlier measurements came from the test harness and not the game, and that the merged tree's whole test suite was not run.
  • The estimate stays at late on Thu 26 Nov. 8.9 is the highest figure merged so far, but it comes from one run on one machine and is short of the 10 frames a second in play, from a long run or a second machine, that this page set as its next mark. An open pull request on the same code reports 131 to 139 ms a frame by default, about 7.2 to 7.6 frames a second.
  • klbf-lab's test page reports a median of 6.6 to 8.4 frames a second in the world at reduced resolution on a Radeon RX 9070 XT, in runs of 14 minutes, and an optional frame generation mode that shows about 17 from about 8.5 rendered. This page counts rendered frames only, and its notes now say so. TuxBox's longest recorded run on Linux is now 18 minutes 11 seconds, with the opening cutscene still not appearing.

item.title: klbf-lab's boats float in a test build, and Belobug's fork draws vehicles and distant trees whole
item.description:
• klbf-lab's README, updated at 11:51 UTC, says a newer test build fixes the water physics that stopped the second mission: with only the throttle held, the boat floated and moved for over a minute before hitting the bank. The project says a full play-through comes next, and the fix is not yet in the version it recommends.
  • VIctory-Belobug-AMD's README, updated at 11:41 UTC, now lists moving vehicles as whole and distant trees as drawn, both broken before. It lists the in-game phone as broken, some draws dropped in the heaviest places, and about 33 GB of memory committed after a quarter of an hour's drive. Its frame rate is unchanged at 3 to 5 frames a second on a Radeon RX 9070 XT.
  • An open pull request on victory-fork measures a small gain on an RTX 4070, in a scene it does not name: sending fetches to a copy queue by default took the frame from 180 to 192 ms down to 174.5 ms, about 5.7 frames a second. It is not merged, and victory-fork's main branch is unchanged since 10:20 UTC.
  • keylime moves from the watch list into the table at stage 5, in 25th place, on its README's report of the intro, main menu and loading screen at 30 frames a second, with no test machine named and no outside report. VIctory-macOS now reports a dark city skyline on an M5 Pro at 0.1 frames a second and says nobody has reached gameplay on a Mac.

item.title: klbf-lab plays further into the second mission, and one more fork joins the table
item.description:
• klbf-lab's README, updated at 11:04 UTC, reports play from the opening mission into the second as far as a seaplane, in a 41-minute session on a test build without a crash, at 5.2 frames a second on average and 12.9 at peak on a Radeon RX 9070 XT. Menus, the map and the HUD now show in that build. Boats, the seaplane and the player in water behave as if there were no water, so those parts were skipped, and the project says it has found the cause and is testing a fix.
  • victory-amd, a fork of victory-fork with fixes for AMD Radeon cards, joins the table at stage 6 in 12th place. Its README reports the opening cutscene and the first room with the player moving at 2 to 3 frames a second on a Radeon RX 7800 XT, in runs of about 8 minutes, tested on one machine.
  • VIctory-macOS reports the game reaching the world on a second Mac, an M5 Pro, as a grey screen at 0.1 frames a second, and loading at 26 to 30 frames a second instead of 8 with new patches. Two projects written from scratch join the watch list: keylime reports the intro, main menu and loading screen at 30 frames a second with no picture in the opening cutscene yet, and gta-vi-astral reports the game running its loop with no 3D picture yet.
  • Forecast review: the estimate stays at late on Thu 26 Nov. klbf-lab's 12.9 is a peak and its average is 5.2, no report reaches 10 frames a second in play from a long run or a second machine, and victory-fork's main branch is unchanged since 10:20 UTC. No new takedown notice names a listed project, and the hourly news sweep found no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two beyond the notice against Leonida.

item.title: Three more public projects join the table, two of them in-game
item.description:
• klbf-lab, a build of VIctory and victory-fork, reports the player in control from the opening mission to the start of the second on a Radeon RX 9070 XT at reduced resolution: 5.7 frames a second while playing, 7.3 standing still over 72 minutes, and 74 minutes in one session without a crash. Its README calls the figures self-reported from one machine. It enters at stage 6 in third place.
  • VIctory-Belobug-AMD, a fork of VIctory for AMD Radeon cards published at 09:41 UTC, reports the world lit and textured at 3 to 5 frames a second on a Radeon RX 9070 XT, with moving vehicles broken and a flat stand-in for ray-traced light. PortWatch, whose owner reports having seen it, ranks it first on its own scale and says it looks close to the retail game. Its README says it is not playable yet. It enters at stage 6 in fourth place.
  • Port of the Americas, a Linux layer, joins at stage 5: its press-start screen, setup pages and loading screens draw, and its world is still black. five-star-recomp's status page says the opening shot's 3D world now reaches the screen through the final composite, in red only. XCL merged 35 pull requests into its main branch between 10:40 and 10:51 UTC with no change to its stated status.
  • The estimate does not move. None of the new figures reaches 10 frames a second in play, and they sit in the same 3 to 7 range as the rest of the field. They add to the evidence that the picture and stability are no longer what holds a playable build back.

item.title: victory-fork merges a measured frame-rate gain, and the estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier
item.description:
• victory-fork's maintainer merged a second batch of frame-rate work at 10:20 UTC. On the maintainer's RTX 4070 the first room went from about 3.5 to 4 frames a second to 4.5 to 5 by default, and to 6 to 7 with every new switch on. The change that lost the graphics device earlier is now in, off by default, with five runs since its fix and no loss.
  • The notes say frame-rate dips remain with no known cause, and that the merged tree's whole test suite was not run. The figures come from one machine and one room.
  • The estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier, to late on Thu 26 Nov, about a day and a half away. A measured gain merged into victory-fork is one of the conditions published at 09:17 UTC. The gain is on a mid-range card and far short of 20, so the move is small. It moves earlier again on 10 or more in play from a long run or a second machine, and later if the gain is withdrawn as unstable or a takedown notice names one of these projects.
  • Builds that take victory-fork's code are picking the work up. ScarlettPort now reports about 4 frames a second in the opening mission on an RTX 3060, up from 2.6, with a frozen overlay over the picture, and VItoriaBr reported up to 6 on an RTX 5060 Ti at 10:10 UTC.

item.title: VItoriaBr reports up to 6 frames a second, and PercyScarlett reaches the opening scene
item.description:
• VItoriaBr's README, changed at 10:10 UTC, reports the open world at 3.5 to 6 frames a second on an RTX 5060 Ti with no driver timeouts, where it gave about 3 before. It had merged victory-fork's 07:30 frame-rate work and several community fixes from 09:31 UTC. It is the first tracked build to publish a gain since that work landed, on a mid-range card, and it is still below the 7.6 measured in a long run on an RTX 4090.
  • PercyScarlett released a v1.0 whose runtime is now built on VIctory, victory-fork and ScarlettPort. Its README says it reaches the opening scene of a title it does not name, lit and textured, at about 2 to 3 frames a second on an RTX 2060 SUPER at reduced resolution, and that speed is far from playable. It says nothing about control there, so it stays at stage 5 and moves to the top of that group, 11th.
  • The estimate does not move. Neither figure reaches 10 frames a second, nobody has confirmed victory-perf's, and victory-fork's own main branch has not moved since 07:30 UTC. The conditions published at 09:17 UTC stand.
  • News check: no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two since the build leaked, and no notice naming another project. VideoCardz has picked up the story, reporting gameplay at 2 to 5 frames a second in unofficial builds and saying projects are moving into private development after the takedown. Of the public repositories this page tests, all but Palmwave still answer.

item.title: Estimate held at its mid-morning review
item.description:
• The mid-morning review leaves the estimate at early on Fri 27 Nov. This was the check for moving it a quarter of a day later if speed had not moved. It has started to: victory-fork merged its first frame-rate work at 07:30 UTC, and its notes name the cost that remains and a change that more than halves it but is not yet stable.
  • It does not move earlier either. Nothing measured in a long run has beaten about 7.6 frames a second since 22:15 UTC on 24 November. victory-perf's 9 to 14 in interiors is still one unconfirmed report, the only other reduced-resolution measurement is 6.1 to 6.4 on an RTX 3090 Ti, and XCL has reported neither control nor a longer run.
  • What moves it next. Earlier by a quarter of a day: a second report of 10 or more in play, a confirmation of victory-perf's figures by someone else, or a measured gain in frame time merged into victory-fork. Later by a quarter of a day: those figures withdrawn or contradicted, or none of the three by the review at about 13:30 UTC.
  • News check: nothing new. Neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has commented since the build leaked. Today's coverage, heise's included, reports the Leonida takedown from the notice GitHub published. No notice names another project, and no outlet has covered or tested victory-perf.

item.title: VIctory-macOS reports the game world on screen on a Mac
item.description:
• VIctory-macOS's README, changed at 08:25 UTC, says that in a later run on one tester's M3 Max the game world appeared on screen before the game's own watchdog stopped it, with frames taking up to 28 seconds while shaders compiled. It is this project's first report of the world on screen on a Mac. It says nothing about control, so it stays at stage 5 and moves up one place to 13th, and the README still says the game is not playable on the Mac.
  • Nothing has moved at the front. victory-fork's main branch is unchanged since 07:30 UTC, VIctory's since 01:36 UTC and XCL's world branch since 07:45 UTC. New pull-request measurements on victory-fork stay at about 4 frames a second on an RTX 3090 Ti, and victory-perf's figures are still unconfirmed.

item.title: ScarlettPort joins the table, and a second reduced-resolution measurement comes in under 7 frames a second
item.description:
• ScarlettPort, a public build of victory-fork's code that this page had not listed, reports the lit world at about 3 to 4 frames a second on an RTX 3060 at reduced resolution, with the keyboard walking the character. Its README does not name the title and says nobody has played a session end to end. It enters the table at stage 6 in sixth place. victory-perf credits it for some of its code.
  • A victory-fork pull request measured the game's lower-resolution mode on an RTX 3090 Ti: 6.1 to 6.4 frames a second, steady, in the opening mission, against 4.7 to 4.8 at full resolution. That supports the direction of victory-perf's report but not its 9 to 14, which nobody else has confirmed. The estimate does not move.
  • News check: neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has commented since the build leaked. TweakTown's report that the Leonida takedown is confirmed rests on the notice GitHub published, and no notice names another project. GameGPU describes footage, credited to a post on X, of boat gameplay on open water at 3 to 5 frames a second, which matches what builds listed here report. No outlet has tested or covered victory-perf.
  • XCL's unmerged world branch gained 17 commits on memory mapping and device handling, with no new frame rate, run length or word on control. victory-fork's main branch has not moved since 07:30 UTC and VIctory's since 01:36 UTC.

item.title: A new fork reports 9 to 14 frames a second in interiors, and victory-fork merges its first frame-rate work
item.description:
• victory-perf, a fork of victory-fork published on the morning of 25 November, reports the opening mission's interiors under player control at 9 to 14 frames a second on an RTX 4070 SUPER, and 4.5 to 6.5 in heavy scenes. The figures are its maintainer's own, from one machine at reduced resolution, with no run length given and shadows lit by stand-ins, and its heavy-scene figure matches what AnyXboxX already reports on the same card.
